She emphasized the importance of directing available resources towards priority interventions in surveillance, laboratory services and the deployment of response personnel. She also underscored the need for quick action and close coordination with the Ministry of Health to ensure that regional support addresses Kenya’s immediate priorities. Principal Secretary Ms. Muthoni welcomed IGAD’s support and highlighted the Ministry’s ongoing contact tracing efforts, while emphasizing the need to strengthen preparedness and surveillance at border points of entry. Recognizing the challenges posed by cross-border population movements to early detection and disease surveillance, she underscored the importance of close coordination between national health authorities and regional partners. She reaffirmed the Government of Kenya’s commitment to continued cooperation with IGAD and expressed readiness to work immediately with the IGAD PREPARE Project to accelerate the implementation of priority Ebola preparedness and response interventions. Kenya’s USD 1 million allocation forms part of the USD 7 million regional Ebola preparedness and response financing endorsed at the Extraordinary IGAD Health Ministerial Meeting on 29 May 2026. Convened under the leadership of IGAD Executive Secretary H.E. Dr Workneh Gebeyehu, the meeting recognized the IGAD Secretariat’s role in coordinating regional preparedness and response and called for emergency activities to be implemented through the Pandemic Fund-supported PREPARE Project. The ministerial commitment established a framework for strengthening surveillance systems, laboratory capacity, health workforce readiness and emergency coordination across seven IGAD Member States. Kenya’s allocation is part of this regional arrangement, connecting its current preparedness priorities to commitments adopted before the imported case was confirmed. The engagement at Afya House builds on that collective commitment. IGAD and Kenya’s Ministry of Health will continue working to align regional preparedness mechanisms with national response efforts, focusing on surveillance, laboratory readiness, rapid response deployment and coordination at points of entry. Timely detection, information sharing and cross-border cooperation remain essential to managing the threat posed by Bundibugyo virus disease and other epidemic-prone diseases. The suspension is ongoing through October 31, 2026 and is likely due to the report of the country’s first Ebola death on October 6. There are no reports yet of any impact to current onboard cruise operations or itineraries from MSC Cruises or any other cruise line. MSC Cruises has temporarily halted Kenyan crew members from boarding its ships at least through October 31, 2026. This decision follows the first-ever imported case of Bundibugyo Ebola in Kenya, which resulted in the death of a Kenyan man who had lived in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) for several years but traveled to Nairobi when ill. The current outbreak began in the DRC in mid-May 2026, and as of October 13, 2026, the CDC reports that 9,000 cases are confirmed with 4,339 confirmed deaths, of which all but three deaths have been in the DRC. According to Kenya’s Ministry of Health, the man, who has not been identified, was isolated at The Nairobi Hospital but died on Monday, October 5. The confirmation of the Bundibugyo Ebola virus was made independently by both the National Virology Reference Laboratory and the Kenya Medical Research Institute (KEMRI) on October 6. The Ministry of Health also notes that contact tracing related to the man’s movements has been strengthened and traveler screening has also been intensified at various points of entry into the country. At this time, no further cases of the Bundibugyo Ebola virus have been reported in Kenya. Because of the outbreak in the DRC and the virulence of the disease, MSC Cruises is being extremely cautious with this action of halting the embarkation of crew members from Kenya. Daily Nation notes that MSC Cruises employs hundreds of crew members from Kenya, though the cruise line has not disclosed how many are currently affected by the pause in bringing Kenyan crew members aboard ships. “As a precautionary measure following recent public health developments in Kenya, MSC Cruises has decided to temporarily suspend the embarkation of Kenyan crew members until 31 October while the situation continues to be monitored and assessed,” the cruise line stated. Workers have reportedly been assured that their employment status, current contracts, and future opportunities with MSC Cruises will not be impacted by the temporary suspension. There has been no information released about Kenyan crew members who may be currently serving onboard MSC Cruises ships or if there may be any alternative plans for them if their contracts are scheduled to end this month. While this is not the first outbreak of the Bundibugyo Ebola virus, the CDC notes that it is the fastest-growing outbreak in history, with more than 1,000 confirmed cases within 40 days of alerts first being raised. In comparison, the most recent large outbreak of a different Ebola strain was in 2018, which took roughly 235 days to surpass 1,000 confirmed cases. Ultimately, the 2018 outbreak had 3,470 cases with 66% mortality. Impact on Cruising MSC Cruises has not made any changes to itineraries or onboard services with respect to the outbreak, but it is possible that some staffing shortages may occur in the next few weeks as the Kenyan crew member suspension continues. No other cruise lines have yet made any announced changes to onboard staffing or operations. Furthermore, neither the Department of State (US) nor Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office (FDCO; UK) have issued high-level warnings about travel to Kenya. The US Department of State lists Kenya as a “Level 2: Exercise Increased Caution” advisory, largely due to crime, kidnapping, civil unrest, and the lack of health care resources. In comparison, the DRC is listed as a “Level 4: Do Not Travel” advisory with the Ebola outbreak cited as the primary concern. The FCDO advises against all travel only to select parts of Kenya and the Democratic Republic of Congo, noting the “highly active, evolving and geographically widespread” Ebola outbreak in the latter. Cruise Hive has reached out to MSC Cruises for a statement but has not yet received a response. 来源:Metabolomics 3.5 编辑推荐: 摘要 引言:埃博拉病毒病(Ebola virus disease,EVD)幸存者在急性疾病消退后常出现临床后遗症,称为后埃博拉综合征(post-Ebola syndrome,PES)。为何部分幸存者出现这些后遗症而其他幸存者未出现,目前尚不明确。急性EVD中已 下载激活素(Activins)海报获取相关药物开发信息。激活素和抑制素是治疗生殖系统疾病的潜在靶点。 为了促进科学的传播,生物通采集了这篇文章 订阅BioHot点这里解锁原文链接推送! “畅读会员”点此登录查看原文链接 Original Article Open access 摘要 引言:埃博拉病毒病(Ebola virus disease,EVD)幸存者在急性疾病消退后常出现临床后遗症,称为后埃博拉综合征(post-Ebola syndrome,PES)。为何部分幸存者出现这些后遗症而其他幸存者未出现,目前尚不明确。急性EVD中已观察到代谢改变,但PES中的代谢改变尚未被研究。在此,研究人员鉴定了伴有PES的EVD幸存者与无症状幸存者相比的独特代谢通路及PES的潜在生物标志物。 目的:本研究旨在确定伴有PES的EVD幸存者是否表现出与无症状EVD幸存者不同的代谢差异。 方法:作为一项正在进行的队列研究的一部分,研究人员收集了塞拉利昂EVD幸存者的血浆。对伴有和不伴有后遗症的幸存者及家庭接触者(household contacts,HCs)进行了非靶向代谢组学(LC-MS/MS)分析。在MetaboAnalyst中进行了单变量、多变量、生物标志物及通路分析。使用JMP进行了Spearman's R相关性分析。 结果:研究人员鉴定了伴有PES的EVD幸存者与无症状幸存者相比,涉及多条代谢通路的代谢物差异表达。这些通路包括三羧酸(tricarboxylic acid,TCA)循环以及氨基酸、核苷酸和短链脂肪酸(short chain fatty acid,SCFA)代谢。其中若干通路与免疫功能障碍相关。所鉴定的代谢物具有作为PES生物标志物的潜在应用价值。 结论:伴有PES的EVD幸存者在多条通路中表现出与无症状EVD幸存者不同的代谢特征。其他研究已将这些通路与免疫功能障碍和慢性病毒感染相关联,但仍需对伴有PES的EVD幸存者进行进一步的免疫代谢研究。 埃博拉病毒病后遗症期的代谢基础:基于血浆代谢组学的系统研究 索取肿瘤靶点蛋白研究最新资料领 取 一、研究背景与科学问题 埃博拉病毒病(Ebola virus disease,EVD)是由埃博拉病毒(Ebola virus,EBOV)引起的高致死性传染病。随着治疗手段的进步,EVD幸存者数量不断增加。然而,相当比例的EVD幸存者在急性感染消退后仍长期遭受多种临床后遗症困扰,这一现象被定义为后埃博拉综合征(post-Ebola syndrome,PES)。PES的临床表现具有高度异质性,涵盖肌肉骨骼、心肺、神经及全身性症状(如头痛、疲劳等),部分症状可在急性病程结束后持续数年之久。尽管PES的临床特征已被广泛描述,但其发病机制仍不清楚,尤其是为何部分幸存者发展为PES而其他幸存者完全无症状,这一关键问题至今缺乏明确解释。 代谢组学作为一种能够系统反映生物体内小分子代谢物整体变化的组学技术,已在多种病毒感染后遗症研究中展现出独特价值。已有研究表明,急性EVD患者存在显著的代谢紊乱,包括血浆游离氨基酸水平下降等;细胞实验亦证实EBOV病毒样颗粒可重编程细胞代谢,影响脂肪酸和氨基酸代谢通路。然而,针对PES的代谢组学研究此前尚属空白。基于此,研究人员提出科学假说:伴有PES的EVD幸存者可能表现出与无症状幸存者不同的独特代谢谱,这些代谢改变可能为PES的发病机制提供新的见解,并可作为潜在的生物标志物。 二、研究设计与核心发现 为验证上述假说,研究人员依托塞拉利昂一项正在进行的EVD幸存者及家庭接触者(household contacts,HCs)队列研究,开展了一项病例对照代谢组学研究。研究纳入三组受试者:伴有PES的EVD幸存者37例(其中肌肉骨骼/胃肠道后遗症18例,心肺后遗症19例)、无症状糖蛋白(glycoprotein,GP)IgG阳性幸存者20例,以及无症状GP IgG阴性家庭接触者20例。各组在年龄、性别、体质指数(body mass index,BMI)及样本采集时间等人口学特征上保持均衡分布。研究人员对血浆样本进行了非靶向液相色谱-串联质谱(LC-MS/MS)代谢组学分析,并通过单变量分析、多变量分析、通路分析及生物标志物分析等多层次统计手段对数据进行挖掘。 研究结果显示,伴有PES的EVD幸存者与无症状幸存者之间存在显著差异的代谢谱。单变量分析共鉴定出544种代谢物,其中34种代谢物在两组间差异表达:26种代谢物在PES组显著下调,8种显著上调。通路分析揭示,PES组呈现以代谢通路下调为主的改变,最显著的下调通路涉及氨基酸代谢(牛磺酸、低牛磺酸、酪氨酸、半胱氨酸和蛋氨酸代谢等),此外核苷酸代谢、三羧酸(tricarboxylic acid,TCA)循环、糖酵解及丙酮酸代谢通路亦显著下调。显著上调的通路包括淀粉和蔗糖代谢、色氨酸代谢、精氨酸和脯氨酸代谢、烟酸和烟酰胺代谢以及戊糖和葡萄糖醛酸相互转化通路。值得注意的是,PES组中短链脂肪酸(short chain fatty acid,SCFA)代谢出现特征性改变:乙酸盐水平升高而丙酸盐水平降低。主成分分析(principal components analysis,PCA)和偏最小二乘判别分析(partial least squares discriminant analysis,PLS-DA)均显示PES组与无症状幸存者组可根据代谢谱实现清晰分离,PLS-DA模型准确率达0.86。 基于上述代谢差异,研究人员进一步开展了生物标志物分析。通过随机森林(Random Forest,RF)和PLS-DA两种独立模型,在发现队列中筛选出10种预测PES的关键代谢物,包括丙烯酸、葡萄糖、乙酸、3-羟基-3-甲基戊二酸、苹果酸、2-氧代-4-羟基-4-羧基-5-脲基咪唑啉、琥珀酸、甲基丙二酸、苏糖酸-1,4-内酯和丙酸。这10种代谢物在两种模型中完全一致,且在独立验证队列中均展现出优异的判别能力,两种模型的曲线下面积(area under the curve,AUC)均大于0.8,验证队列的预测准确率分别为0.799(PLS-DA)和0.796(RF)。此外,Spearman相关性分析显示PES组内TCA循环、氨基酸、脂肪酸和核苷酸代谢通路之间存在显著的相关网络,进一步支持这些代谢通路间的协同改变。 三、研究意义与展望 本研究首次系统描绘了PES患者的血浆代谢组学特征,揭示了PES与多条代谢通路的下调密切相关,特别是TCA循环、氨基酸代谢和核苷酸代谢的改变,与慢性病毒感染(如HIV)中观察到的线粒体功能障碍和T细胞耗竭现象具有一致性。SCFA代谢的改变则提示PES患者可能存在肠道微生态失调,这一发现与长新冠(Long COVID)研究中的观察相呼应。研究鉴定的10种代谢物组合在独立验证队列中展现出稳定的预测效能,为PES的早期识别和风险分层提供了潜在的生物标志物工具。 研究人员指出,本研究存在若干局限性:样本量相对有限,可能遗漏部分关键代谢物;研究仅聚焦于肌肉骨骼/胃肠道和心肺两类后遗症亚组,限制了结果向更广泛PES表型的推广;缺乏急性期代谢数据及纵向随访样本,难以区分持续性代谢改变与PES特异性改变;血浆样本无法直接反映细胞水平的代谢机制。未来研究需要在更大样本中验证上述发现,开展细胞水平的免疫代谢机制研究,并与其它病毒感染后遗症(如SARS-CoV-2)进行直接代谢组学比较,以确定这些代谢改变的临床相关性和普适性。 四、研究结论 EVD幸存者在TCA循环、氨基酸、核苷酸及短链脂肪酸代谢通路中表现出显著改变的代谢特征。其中若干通路已在其它病毒感染研究中被证实与免疫功能障碍(尤其是CD8+ T细胞功能)及慢性感染密切相关。基于现有数据,任何关于病毒持续存在的推测均仅为假设。仍需对伴有PES的EVD幸存者开展细胞水平的免疫代谢研究,并与其它病毒感染后遗症进行直接代谢组学比较,以确定研究发现的临床意义。 打赏 records.content: MENU Home Business Columns Finance Lifestyle Zoom News Editorial team Home Business Columns Finance Lifestyle Zoom News Editorial team South Sudan strengthens Ebola surveillance after Kenya confirms imported case October 7, 2026 Pawla Nibramich News 0 South Sudan has heightened nationwide Ebola preparedness and surveillance after neighboring Kenya confirmed an imported case caused by the Bundibugyo virus, the Ministry of Health said on Wednesday. No cases have been detected in South Sudan, but authorities have placed the health system on high alert amid concerns over cross-border movement and trade routes linking the country to affected areas in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Kenya and Uganda. Caretaker Health Minister Dak Duop Bichiok said screening had been activated at entry points, across 15 high-risk border counties and at Juba International Airport. A national task force is coordinating preparedness operations, while eight specialised infectious disease units have been established for isolation and treatment should cases be confirmed. World Health Organization representative Moses Ongom said South Sudan’s response preparedness had risen from 29 per cent in May and 45 per cent in June to 65 per cent currently. The Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention said surveillance, laboratory testing and rapid response systems were operational, with regional coordination support based in Kampala.
